# Q10 quest handlers (pandaemonium, altgard): deviations and generated files

## P6-Q slice 2, lane Q10 (2026-09-29)

The 75 Java handlers of `game-server/data/handlers/quest/altgard` (32) and `pandaemonium` (43), the zones a new Asmodian Daeva reaches after
the ascension route (the dispatch quests 2901-2904 and 29070/29071 end in Altgard). Worktree `route-hand`, branch `p6q/q10` (based on C++
`a72676184`), build dir `cpp/build/rh`; uncommitted for the integrator. Method: docs/design/p6q-ascension-route.md (questgen emit and copy,
`AION_QUEST_HANDLER` markers, generator fixes in `tools/gen` rather than hand edits, the golden trace harness, `tools/parity`); owner rules
U1/U7 (docs/design/owner-decisions.md).

| | Files |
|---|---|
| Generated by questgen (bannered, drift-tested) | **69**: altgard 28, pandaemonium 41 |
| Hand-ported (statement by statement) | **5**: altgard `_2208MauInTenMinutesADay`, `_2230AFriendlyWager`, `_2252ChasingtheLegend`, `_24013PoisonInTheWaters`; pandaemonium `_2900NoEscapingDestiny` |
| Held back | **1**: pandaemonium `_4212MissingSidrunerk` (an unported engine package on its path, below; not a gate) |
| Landed with an unported engine body on the path (the review of 2026-09-29) | **4**: altgard `_2284EscapingAsmodae`, `_2290GrokensEscape` (generated), pandaemonium `_2900NoEscapingDestiny` (hand port), `_2985AnExpertsReward` (generated): each can be accepted but not completed until a phase-5 body is ported; below, "Landed with an unported engine body on the path" |

**Integration of slice 2** (docs/design/p6q-ascension-route.md, "Slice 2"): 16 of the 69 generated files are held back for their
gs.scenario.travel traffic (section "Held back"): 53 generated (altgard 18, pandaemonium 35) and 5 hand ports are in the tree.

Every file is in `cpp/game-server/handlers/aion/gameserver/handlers/quest/<dir>/`, compiled into `aion_gs_handlers_quest_q10`, and registers
with `AION_QUEST_HANDLER`. Every gate server logs "Loaded 4300 quest handlers" (4,226 + 74).

### Generator changes

Two compile fixes, both additive (an include the emitted file lacked), both in the emitter's include logic:

| Change | Where | Why |
|---|---|---|
| A call whose C++ result is a `runtime::Ref<T>` includes T's header: `api.header_of(T)`, else the new table `api.OWNED_RESULT_HEADERS` (`Effect` -> `skillengine/model/Effect.h`, the only entry) | `emit.ret_type`, `api.OWNED_RESULT_HEADERS` | `_2213PoisonRootPotentFruit.java:74` discards `SkillEngine.getInstance().applyEffectDirectly(...)`; the discarded `Ref<Effect>` is destroyed by the caller, which needs the complete type (C2027 in `Ref.h`) |
| A pointer dereferenced for a `T&` parameter (the idiom "pointer dereferenced for a T& parameter") includes its class's header | `emit.convert` (`self.need(e.ct.name)`) | `_2223AMythicalMonster.java:108` passes `env.getPlayer().getWorldMapInstance()` to `spawnForFiveMinutes(..., WorldMapInstance&, ...)`; `Ptr<WorldMapInstance>::operator*` needs the complete type |

Effect on the whole corpus (`python -m tools.gen.questgen --dry-run --emit <dir>` before and after, then `diff -rq`): **29 of the 929 emitted
files** (of 1,035 Java handlers) change, each by added `#include` lines only (15 `WorldMapInstance.h`, 10 `WorldPosition.h`, 4
`skillengine/model/Effect.h`): altgard `_2213`, `_2223`; bare_truth `_14030`; beluslan `_2600`, `_28602`; black_cloud_traders `_39505`,
`_39510`, `_39515`, `_39520`; clash_of_destiny `_24031`; cygnea `_10506`, `_10507`; enshar `_20501`, `_20503`, `_20504`, `_20507`, `_25050`,
`_25051`, `_25052`; gelkmaros `_21105`, `_21249`; heiron `_1636`, `_1647`, `_18602`; inggison `_10031`; morheim `_2343`; sanctum `_3908`;
theobomos `_3082`; verteron `_14016`. None of the 32 route files of slice 1 changes. The count stays 929 of 1,035, and **all 929 are at
parity** (`parity.py tree` over the emitted corpus: 929 pairs compared, 0 with mismatches). Four of the changed files are in heiron/verteron,
the other slice-2 lane's chunk; the integrator re-runs the generator over every landed chunk. Tests: `test_questgen_tree.py`
`test_the_slice_two_include_rules` (both rules on 2213 and 2223, and no include for 2207, which needs neither) and the drift test; the
`tools.gen` suite passes (below).

### Hand ports

All five follow the questgen output's conventions (the class in the directory's namespace, `AION_QUEST_HANDLER` last, Java statement order and
literals, step comments kept). Each file started from questgen's own output for a copy of the Java with the refused construct neutralized
(outside the repository), then the construct was written by hand, so the rest is byte for byte what the generator writes. **None has a
deviation from Java.**

| File | Why questgen refuses it | How the refused construct is ported |
|---|---|---|
| `altgard/_2208MauInTenMinutesADay.cpp` | the anonymous `Runnable` of `:85` | A pinned task (fieldmap `_2208MauInTenMinutesADay$1`, storage: task): `schedule({this, &user, &state, &env}, [...], 3000)`; its captures (the handler, Immortal under RT-11; the player; the quest state; the env) are the Pin, `id` and `itemObjId` are copied |
| `altgard/_2230AFriendlyWager.cpp` | `CreatureController.hasTask` / `cancelTask` (not in questgen's API table) | Direct: `player->getController().hasTask(TaskId::QUEST_TIMER)` and `cancelTask(TaskId::QUEST_TIMER)` (CreatureController.h:163, :171; both ported) |
| `altgard/_2252ChasingtheLegend.cpp` | `WorldMapInstance.getNpcs`, `PacketSendUtility.broadcastMessage` (not in the table) | Direct: `getNpcs({questKillNpc1Id, questKillNpc2Id}).empty()` (the `int...` overload, WorldMapInstance.h:137) and `PacketSendUtility::broadcastMessage(questMob, 1100630, 500)` (PacketSendUtility.h:87) |
| `altgard/_24013PoisonInTheWaters.cpp` | the lambda of `:85` | A pinned task (fieldmap `_24013PoisonInTheWaters@L85:45`): `schedule({this, &env, &user}, [...], 3000)`, the handler (for `spawn`), the env and the player |
| `pandaemonium/_2900NoEscapingDestiny.cpp` | the `throw` of `:259`; `Equipment.unEquipItem` (not in the table) | `throw runtime::UnsupportedOperationException("Unhandled player class " + std::string(xml::enumName(...)))` (Java's `+ player.getPlayerClass()` is the enum's name); `player->getEquipment().unEquipItem(item->getObjectId())` (Equipment.h:62, ported) |

Parity (`parity.py pair <java> <cpp>`): 2208, 2230, 2252 and 24013 are at parity (the `Runnable`/lambda spellings of the P6-Q integration).
**2900 has two mismatches** (calls multiset and order: `string`, `enumName`): Java's string concatenation converts the enum implicitly, the C++
names the conversion. Every literal, DialogAction, other call and spawn id matches. Decision for the integrator: a documented tools/parity
spelling ("`std::string(xml::enumName(x))` inside a string concatenation is Java's implicit `toString`"), as the integration of slice 1 did
for the `Runnable` of 1002/2002/2136.

Java behaviour kept as it is (no `// java-bug kept` marker; none is in phase6-inventory.md §11):

- 2252's `QUEST_SELECT` at var 0 answers page 2034 only when `giveQuestItem` answers false, which it never does for a constant item and count
  (AbstractQuestHandler.java:626-641): page 1693 at every talk. `giveQuestItem` gives the bones only when none is held; with the bones held it
  sends STR_CAN_NOT_GET_LORE_ITEM and still answers true (corrected by the review of 2026-09-29: this line said every talk gives another bone).
  `USE_OBJECT` removes the bones item (`checkItemExistence(..., true)`) and falls out of the switch: the hook answers false even when it spawned
  a legend.
- 2208's item hook checks neither the status nor the var: a use in REWARD sets var 1 again three seconds later.
- 2230's logout and timer-end hooks act only in START; `abandonQuest` deletes a never-completed 2230.
- 2900's `getStoneId` throws for a starting class (`UnsupportedOperationException`), so its death and enter-world hooks throw for a
  character below the ascension; the quest is LOCKED from level 18 and starts at level 20 (`defaultOnLevelChangedEvent` checks a mission's
  start conditions 2 levels early and adds it LOCKED below its level, AbstractQuestHandler.java:988-1030; corrected by the review, this line
  said it starts at 18), so only a data error reaches the throw.

### Landed with an unported engine body on the path

Found by the review of 2026-09-29 (the mutation review named 2284 and 2290; the harness's new AION_UNPORTED tally and the unit cases found 2900
and 2985). Each file compiles and transliterates (or ports) its Java faithfully, and calls ported code, but a phase-5 body its path reaches at
run time is `AION_UNPORTED`: the body throws UnportedException (counted in the unported trace), which QuestEngine.onDialog catches and logs
("QE: exception in onDialog"; 2900's equip throws in the item's equip path instead), and the quest cannot be completed until the body is
ported. No handler change is needed then.

| Quest | Where the path stops | The unported body (owner) | What a player sees |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2284 Escaping Asmodae (generated) | SETPRO3 at 798041, the escort (`defaultStartFollowEvent`, Java :54) | `AbstractQuestHandler::defaultStartFollowEvent` (AbstractQuestHandler.cpp:817-826): needs `questEngine/task`, m5d-plan.md E-07 | accepted; var 1 is the last step reached |
| 2290 Groken's Escape (generated) | SELECT1_1 at the start (`startQuest`, then the escort) and QUEST_SELECT at var 0 at 203608 | the same | started at the accept, then the escort throws at every talk; 2222 cannot start |
| 2900 No Escaping Destiny (hand port) | the stigma stone's equip at var 99 (the step 99 -> 97 is `onEquipItemEvent`, after the equip) | `StigmaService::getPossibleStigmaCount` and `addStigmaSkills` (Equipment.equipItem -> `StigmaService::notifyEquipAction`); `removeStigma`'s unequip of an equipped stone reaches `StigmaService::removeStigmaSkills` (StigmaService.cpp:189-216) | the stone is given; equipping it throws, so the quest stays at 99 (a death or a return takes the stone back to step 4, which works: nothing is equipped) |
| 2985 An Expert's Reward (generated) | the finish (`sendQuestEndDialog` -> `QuestService::finishQuest`) | `WarehouseService::expand` (WarehouseService.cpp:29; the reward `extend_inventory="2"`, QuestService.cpp:386-387) | the finish gives the reward's 291,412 exp, then throws before COMPLETE: the quest stays REWARD, and **every retry gives the exp again**. Reaching it needs one of the expert crafting quests 2931-2934 finished (level 29, crafting at 399), which no play session is near; the exp repeat is an engine gap of `finishQuest` (every `extend_inventory="2"` quest, 2 in quest_data.xml), reported here for the owner |

Why landed and not held back like 4212: 4212 cannot be written at all (`QuestTasks.newFollowingToTargetCheckTask` has no C++ declaration;
questgen refuses it), while these four compile against ported declarations and start working when the phase-5 bodies land, as slice 1's
1006/2008 landed with the unported `AbyssPointsService::addAp` on their kill path (p6q-ascension-route.md §5 item 2); the
task holds a handler back only for its gate impact, and none of the four reaches a gate (levels 12 to 29). Holding them back is the
integrator's alternative (2284, 2290 and 2985: the regenerate command in reverse; 2900: the hand port would have to be kept outside the tree).
The golden harness lists 2985's reach in `knownUnported` (GoldenQuestTraceTest.cpp); the oracle refuses the two follow hooks; 2900's equip
has no unit case (it would pin a phase-5 `AION_UNPORTED`).

(1,857 s; the verify tree ran its own gates on the same machine meanwhile): **51 of 51 passed** (63 entries, 12 disabled gtest shadows). Times
(s): smoke.startup 32.7, smoke.startup_progress 32.5, smoke.startup_geo 155, m5a 60, m5a_geo 164, m5b 234, m5b_geo 341, m5b2 259, m5b2_geo
294, m5b3 158, m5b3_geo 411, m5c 335, travel 45, ascension 909. The worktree has no `game-server/config/mygs.properties`, so
`gameserver.simple.secondclass.enable` is false and 1006/2008/1007/2009 register too. Error lines: none in any gate server log except
gs.scenario.ascension's 10 "onDie() exception" of the unported `AbyssPointsService::addAp` (p6q-ascension-route.md §5 item 2, unchanged).

  teleporter) gains quest talk registrations (2953 and 2954); the travel gate passes with them.

The review of 2026-09-29 changed no handler, generator or manifest file (each has the lane's sha256; the changes are test and tool code),
so the gate run above stands; 24010's enter-world start, the one hook the travel gate reaches, now has a unit case of its own (below). On the
review's rebuild (every target, 0 errors, 0 warnings) gs.smoke.startup (31 s) and gs.scenario.travel (45 s) were run again: both passed.

  `tools/oracle/expected/quest/<id>.json` (1,521 cases, 23 high ends, 32 hooks refused over the whole slice, 24 of them Q10's); no committed
  trace of slice 1 changed (the review added one field to 32 of them, below). 8 documents have every hook refused (2213, 2925, 2938, 2952,
  4966-4969; `ORACLE_REFUSES_EVERY_HOOK`): only their registration traces are checked by the harness.
- The table (`GoldenHandlers.h`, 69 rows) and `GoldenAltgardHandlers.cpp` / `GoldenPandaemoniumHandlers.cpp` (the `#include` lists).
- What the harness had to learn for these traces (each a model of the Java, none a relaxation): the hooks `onLogOutEvent`,
  `onQuestTimerEndEvent`, `onAtDistanceEvent`, `onGetItemEvent`, `onDieEvent`; an item hook's `given.item.itemId` (0 is an item no guard
  names: `OTHER_ITEM`, 182200201); the replay of `sendQuestStartDialog(item, count)`, `changeQuestStep(step, next)`,
  `QuestService.abandonQuest`, `useQuestObject` (4 and 10 arguments), the one-npc `defaultOnKillEvent` overloads, `defaultCloseDialog`'s six
  ints and `defaultOnGetItemEvent`; the item rows of every nine-digit effect argument (an item a helper gives beside its step); the real
  `player_experience_table.xml` (quests up to level 50); two overlays (a path that reads no QuestState gets one START at its step helper's
  step, with the kill helper's npc as the target; a start helper gets the quest's prerequisites finished); in the registration trace the
  calls `registerOnLogOut`, `registerOnQuestTimerEnd`, `registerOnDie`, `registerOnGetItem`, `registerAddOnReach/LostTargetEvent`,
  `addHandlerSideQuestDrop` (counted in QuestService's drop table) and the set semantics of every `QuestNpc.addOn*` (`_2213` registers
  203604's talk twice; QuestNpc.java keeps it once).
- Result: **106 of 106 tests** (37 before; the 69 new ones are `Generated/GoldenQuestCases` instances); for Q10 **1,539 of 1,544** variants pass
  (1,521 cases + 23 high ends), 0 fail, 5 listed not reproducible (`knownNotReproducible`: 4210 onKillEvent#1/#2, whose base state cannot
  make a kill helper true while an overlay reproduces and compares it; 2223 onDialogEvent#21 and 24012 onDialogEvent#12 with its high end,
  whose `useQuestObject` kills the target, which the pair of runs cannot share, covered below). 162 vacuous cases are listed with their reasons
  (`GoldenKnownVacuousQ10.h`: 105 `sendQuestStartDialog` at USE_OBJECT, 54 `sendQuestEndDialog` outside REWARD with a reward action, 2
  `defaultCloseDialog` off its step, 1 kill pair assumed false). Slice 1 still passes all its cases; its four "startQuest assumed false"
  vacuous entries of 2114 left the list, observable now through the prerequisites overlay.
- **The review of 2026-09-29** (M5, M8 and M9 of the review table below):
  - *Free-dialog overlays.* The oracle now writes `dialogExcludes` on a case whose path reads the dialog action only through `!=` guards (the
    else branch of `if (action == QUEST_SELECT) ... else return sendQuestStartDialog(env)`, a switch's default): the excluded action ids
    (`Extractor.dialog_excludes`; none when the path writes the action or uses it in an effect argument or the return value). Any action
    outside the list takes the same path with the same effects, so the harness runs the case with each action the start and end helpers act

    also with the quest's first permitted class and its start prerequisites finished. 858 of the 2,245 cases of the 105 documents carry the
    list; regenerating added the field to 32 of the 36 slice-1 documents as well and changed nothing else in them (`git diff`: 141
    insertions, no other line).
    Every case still passes: for Q10 1,539 of 1,544 variants, 0 failed, 5 not reproducible as before, now in 8,079 compared runs (2,409
    without the new overlays); slice 1 781 in 2,859 (1,814). 122 of the 162 Q10 vacuous entries are observable now and left the list (all
